transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-10-16
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Claire Jensen (Redwood AE), Marcus Liu (Redwood CSM), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Janelle Ortiz (SentinelRx Head of ML), Derek Nguyen (SentinelRx Platform Eng), Priya Rao (CTO), Carlos Menendez (Security Lead)

Summary: Quick kickoff to align on pilot scope, security gating, infra choice (we discussed Redwood hosted, Dedicated, and Private/VPC), and immediate artifacts needed to get a pilot running. Some audio glitches mid-call, a few words mis-transcribed.

Topics: pilot success criteria, latency SLOs, data residency, KMS + key management, runbook & staging access, cost modelling for burst traffic, canary/rollback plan.

[00:00] Claire Jensen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Claire from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, quick intro round please
[00:08] Janelle Ortiz: hi all, Janelle here, head of ml at SentinelRx, mostly focused on inference quality and evals
[00:12] Derek Nguyen: Derek, platform eng, i'll own networking and deployment pieces
[00:15] Priya Rao: Priya, CTO, excited to get this moving
[00:18] Carlos Menendez: Carlos, security lead, i'll be the audit person for SOC2/KMS questions
[00:22] Marcus Liu: Marcus, customer success at Redwood, i'll be shepherding the runbook and timeline
[00:27] Samir Patel: Samir, solutions eng, i'll dig into latency, batching, and the benchmark plan

[02:00] Claire Jensen: objective today is a short intake — align pilot goals, blockers, and immediate owners. i know you sent over the initial use cases Janelle, can you recap the top two we should focus on?
[02:15] Janelle Ortiz: sure. number one is prescription reconciliation assistant — we need sub-300ms completion for short prompts, and must maintain F1 above our baseline on entity extraction. number two is post-visit summarization for clinicians, that's longer form but throughput is higher tolerance up to 2s per completion. both have PHI mix so data handling is critical

[04:10] Samir Patel: got it. so two different profiles — short-latency, low-context vs longer context, higher throughput. for the short-latency path we typically recommend Dedicated or Hosted with edge routing; private on-prem can work but you'll see higher ops overhead.
[04:32] Derek Nguyen: can you expand on the ops overhead for private? we might want VPC-hosted not full on-prem
[04:36] Samir Patel: yeah, with Private (VPC) you manage the worker nodes and networking, so our control plane talks over secured peering, but keys stay customer-controlled. it's great for compliance but we ask for some infra config time — typically extra 2-3 weeks for networking and HSM/KMS integration

[06:05] Carlos Menendez: on KMS — we require customer-managed keys or HSM-backed KMS for the pilot. does Redwood support CMEK today?
[06:12] Marcus Liu: short answer yes, we support CMEK with our Private deployments and Dedicated via bring-your-key (BYOK) patterns. there are a couple of steps we'll share in the wiring doc.
[06:26] Claire Jensen: we'll attach the KMS integration checklist after the call. also note SOC 2 attestation, we can share our certs and audit artifacts.

[07:30] Priya Rao: timeline wise, our Q4 target is to have a pilot that can take real traffic from a small cohort of clinics. what's realistic?
[07:40] Marcus Liu: if we go Hosted pilot, we can be live in ~1 week with a limited capacity pilot; Dedicated or Private will add lead time — Dedicated maybe 2–3 weeks depending on commit, Private closer to 3–5 weeks because of network and HSM tasks.

[09:00] Janelle Ortiz: for evaluation we need reproducible benchmarks and quality gating. can you recommend a metric set?
[09:06] Samir Patel: absolutely — we'll propose a benchmark with latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), token cost per request, and task-specific quality metrics — e.g., slot F1 for reconciliation and ROUGE/BLEU for summaries. we'll also include KV cache warmup behavior for multi-turn flows

[11:10] Derek Nguyen: about networking: we prefer to keep egress minimal, requires explicit egress allowlist — can you provide the CIDR ranges and ports?
[11:20] Samir Patel: yes, we'll provide a compact egress/ingress spec. for Private we'll do VPC peering and private link, for Hosted we'll need IP allowlist for webhooks if you plan callbacks to internal services.

[12:50] Carlos Menendez: any thoughts on data residency? some of our clinics are in EU — we need data not to transit or be stored outside region.
[12:58] Claire Jensen: Redwood supports region pinning in hosted for many regions, and Private naturally runs in your region. for the pilot we can pin to the west-eu region or run a Dedicated pool in the EU, we will confirm model availability for each region in the catalog doc

[14:35] Priya Rao: cost — we've been comparing cost profiles for Redwood vs other vendors. for short-latency path we don't want to blow up monthly cost as traffic scales. how do we control that?
[14:45] Marcus Liu: a few levers: batching config for the longer summarization path, prefix caching for multi-turn flows, and quantization profiles for model selection. Optimize (our toolkit) will propose config to balance cost/latency after we see your token distribution.

[16:30] Janelle Ortiz: what's the SLA for Dedicated? we need 99.9 uptime for the pilot.
[16:35] Claire Jensen: Dedicated is available with SLA options; we'll include the SLA terms in the pricing doc. for pilot we often accept 99.5 while we ramp, but we can update contract terms for production.

[18:05] Derek Nguyen: are there sample runbooks? we want detailed playbooks for failover and rollback during canaries.
[18:12] Marcus Liu: yes, Marcus: i'll share our staging runbook — includes canary steps, rollback, emergency key rotation, and observability hooks (tracing and per-route latency).

[19:40] Samir Patel: a technical note — for the reconciliation assistant short prompts, late-binding KV cache and attention kernel choice matter. we saw up to 30% lower p95 with reduced kv hop optimization on certain open models. i'll include a kernel profile sample in the benchmark bundle

[21:30] Janelle Ortiz: perfect. also we need to ensure all logs with PHI are redacted or never stored — what does Redwood persist by default?
[21:40] Claire Jensen: default retention is 30 days for logs in Hosted with options to disable or redact; Dedicated/Private gives you control over retention and whether telemetry leaves the VPC. we'll note the default telemetry flow in the security doc

[23:00] Carlos Menendez: can we get a copy of the data flow diagram and the SOC2 report after the call?
[23:06] Marcus Liu: yes we'll attach SOC2 type II report and a data flow diagram. i'll mark that action

[24:10] Priya Rao: what's your recommended pilot size for realistic traffic?
[24:18] Samir Patel: start small — 5 clinics producing bursts across business hours. for latency validation focus on 5000 short requests and 500 long summaries across a week, that gives good signal for p95 and cost modeling.

[26:00] Claire Jensen: let's talk about decision owners — Priya will sign off on production readiness, Janelle will own quality gating, Derek will own networking, Carlos will be the security approver. is that good?
[26:10] Priya Rao: yes that works
[26:15] Janelle Ortiz: yes

[28:00] Marcus Liu: i'll draft a 4-week pilot plan: week 0 staging wiring, week 1 smoke + latency bench, week 2 small clinic roll, week 3 widen and evaluate, then a sign-off meeting.

[29:10] Derek Nguyen: one more question on telemetry — do you provide token-level cost breakdown by route?
[29:18] Samir Patel: yes token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route in Console, plus per-model dashboards. you can also export traces to your observability stack

[31:05] Carlos Menendez: any red-team style review for the infra? we might run a compliance scan before we go live
[31:12] Claire Jensen: you can schedule a security review, we also provide penetration test reports; for Private deployments we can support in-person audits under NDA if needed

[33:00] Janelle Ortiz: ok let's recap real quick, owners and artifacts: Redwood shares runbook, KMS checklist, egress spec, SOC2 report, and benchmark scripts. SentinelRx provides network diagram, sample anonymized datasets, and final list of clinic IDs for pilot.

[34:20] Marcus Liu: i'll email a consolidated action list right after this, and create a shared staging folder with access controls

[35:55] Claire Jensen: scheduling — when is good for the SE deep-dive? week of 10/19?
[36:02] Derek Nguyen: week of 10/19 is good for me, prefer morning PT
[36:08] Janelle Ortiz: same, mornings are better

[37:20] Priya Rao: any blockers from Redwood's side to starting a Hosted pilot immediately?
[37:26] Claire Jensen: no blockers for Hosted, we just need dataset and credentials for staging webhooks; Dedicated/Private need contract and network steps

[38:40] Marcus Liu: next steps recap in bullets: share staging runbook (Marcus), benchmark bundle (Samir), pricing options (Claire), network diagram from SentinelRx (Derek & team).

[40:10] Carlos Menendez: thanks all, we'll review SOC2 and KMS steps and get the diagram to you by the 20th
[40:20] Janelle Ortiz: thanks everyone, excited to get started
[40:30] Claire Jensen: thanks Sentinels, we'll follow up with docs and schedule, talk soon

End of transcript.
